idiom_name: tonic service trait generated from .proto (+ Cargo semver for crate-shaped consumers)
implementation_notes: Rust has no standard-library HTTP or RPC server, so the protocol is published with tonic: build.rs compiles the .proto, generating the message structs and the service trait, and the implementation of that trait is the host service - the generated types are the published language and the domain types stay private behind pub(crate) and a mapper. Evolution follows protobuf's rules (add fields, never renumber or remove). When the consumers are Rust crates rather than remote clients, the same pattern is the crate's public API plus Cargo's semver contract: what counts as a breaking change is documented by the Cargo reference, so a major-version bump is the versioned contract and pub(crate) is what keeps internals unpublished.
pitfalls: Generated protobuf structs are plain data; letting them become the domain model makes every internal refactor a schema change.
Exported items are permanently public: without pub(crate) an accidental pub freezes an internal type into the crate's contract, and Cargo's semver rules then forbid changing it incompatibly.
Blocking or CPU-heavy work inside an async tonic handler starves the runtime; move it to spawn_blocking or a bounded pool.
